articles.excerpt: DVC inventory should follow remotes and credential files Data Version Control, or DVC, manages data and model files through Git-like metadata while storing the actual content in remotes such as S3, Az…
articles.body: DVC inventory should follow remotes and credential files Data Version Control, or DVC, manages data and model files through Git-like metadata while storing the actual content in remotes such as S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage, SSH, SFTP, HTTP, WebDAV, HDFS, or local directories. A DVC application fingerprint is therefore not a reliable proxy for the data exposure. The important assets are the configured remotes and the credentials used to reach them. Measurement On 2026-11-03 UTC, ZoomEye was queried with page 1, pagesize=1 , and sub_type=all . app="DVC" returned 16 observations. title="DVC" returned 802. The application count is a small set of observable matches. The title count is broad and may include documentation, tutorials, and unrelated uses of the acronym.

articles.title: Build a Redirect Map Before a Website Redesign
articles.excerpt: A website redesign can improve navigation, readability and conversion paths, but it can also break years of accumulated links in one afternoon. The risk is not the new visual design itself. The risk a…
articles.body: A website redesign can improve navigation, readability and conversion paths, but it can also break years of accumulated links in one afternoon. The risk is not the new visual design itself. The risk appears when old URLs disappear, change meaning or point visitors to a generic page without a plan. A redirect map is the handover document that connects every important old URL to its best new destination. Build it before launch, not after customers and search engines begin finding errors. Start with an inventory of real URLs Do not create the map from the new sitemap alone. Collect URLs from the existing XML sitemap, analytics landing pages, Search Console landing pages, internal links, campaign links, downloadable files and any high-value external references you know about.

articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.excerpt: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Tele…
articles.body: New research suggests that collisions between stars in the early universe were common, which could help explain the rapid growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). The team behind this research performed simulations of the early universe and found stellar systems were densely packed, leading to stars frequently slamming into each other. While rapid collisions would have destroyed the stars involved, slower collisions would have led to repeated mergers, creating single over-massive stars, which could collapse and form larger-than-usual black holes at the end of their lives. These could be the seeds of the first supermassive black holes.

articles.title: These muscle-reading wearables let you use voice input without speaking a word
articles.excerpt: Forget glide typing — these glasses have maybe the best text-entry trick yet.
articles.body: TL;DR Subvocal’s glasses tech uses radar to analyze the movement of muscles in your mouth. From those readings, it can extrapolate the words you’re saying — even if you’re just silently mouthing them. Pre-orders for the wearable are open now, with orders expected to ship in Q1 2027. Ever since mobile devices started getting smaller than a laptop, engineers have been tackling the difficult question of how we’re supposed to enter text. We’ve gone from tiny physical keyboards , to touchscreen keyboards, to gesture-based glide typing . On wearables, the situation’s even trickier, and it can feel like we’re stuck either using voice input or left awkwardly poking in the air at a virtual keyboard. But now one startup has a clever, hands-free solution that works silently.

articles.body: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement .

articles.title: Hubble Telescope sees cosmic 'cat's tail' that could wrap around Earth and the sun 500 times
articles.excerpt: Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail formed when two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together.
articles.body: Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together. The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats. The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old , Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old.

articles.title: OpenAI seems to be silently re-enabling model training on Codex chats
articles.excerpt: My company is pretty paranoid about leaking IP to the frontier labs through prompts, so we've all been diligent about disabling data sharing in Codex/Claude Code/etc. But yesterday my coworkers and I…
articles.body: My company is pretty paranoid about leaking IP to the frontier labs through prompts, so we've all been diligent about disabling data sharing in Codex/Claude Code/etc. But yesterday my coworkers and I noticed that the setting had been silently reenabled in Codex. None of us knowingly opted back in. You can check your settings here: https://chatgpt.com/settings/data-controls. Look for "Improve the model for everyone". Curious if this is an isolated issue or something more widespread. EDIT: looks like this has been noted before https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49643556 EDIT: apparently you can also turn off data sharing here: https://privacy.openai.com/policies?modal=take-control
